findings.statement: Rank one in the convergence ranking and strongly tumour-up in TCGA (purity-robust). Open Targets association is mostly literature-driven, with no genetic or somatic evidence. Tractable by antibody, small molecule and PROTAC; cell membrane (microvillus) protein, so it is also a measurable biomarker. Drugs: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. ccRCC lines are not dependent on it (DepMap selectivity [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.031]), and it is not a recurrently mutated gene. PRISM best compound is para-toluenesulfonamide, which has several targets and is not significant. So CA9 is a surface-antigen / imaging / ADC-type target and biomarker, not a dependency target.

Convergence rank four; tumour-up, purity-robust. Cell-membrane TNF-family ligand (CD27 ligand). Tractable by antibody and other clinical modalities (Open Targets: Advanced Clinical). Drugs: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. No ccRCC dependency (not selective, not common essential), so the case rests on surface expression for ADC, antibody or cell therapy, not on a dependency.

Convergence rank eight and the top biomarker-profile score among the leaders. Strongly tumour-up, purity-robust, with adverse prognosis and a grade association in TCGA survival. Cytoplasmic enzyme (methyl-donor / SAM consumption), so not an antibody target. Small-molecule tractable (druggable family, high-quality ligand) but no clinical drug listed. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (slightly negative selectivity), so it is an untested tractable gene and a prognostic biomarker, not a validated target.

Convergence rank six; the highest target-profile score of the leaders. Tumour-up, purity-robust; the only leading gene with a genetic-association component in Open Targets. Cell membrane and caveola receptor (HDL uptake), antibody and small-molecule tractable, but no drug is listed. No ccRCC dependency in DepMap, so tractable but untested and a weaker target case.

Convergence rank two. Very strongly tumour-up in RNA and protein, purity-robust. It is a hypoxia-associated cytochrome c oxidase subunit with minimal Open Targets association. The listed drugs (ME-344 PHASE_1_2, METFORMIN WITHDRAWAL) are not selective for this gene. Tractability is only an approved-drug annotation, and there is no ccRCC dependency. Best treated as a biomarker candidate.

Convergence rank three; strongly down in tumour (proximal tubule marker lost), with favourable prognosis in TCGA survival. No drugs and no dependency. It is a loss-of-expression diagnostic and prognostic biomarker, not a target.

Convergence rank five; strongly down in tumour with a favourable prognostic signal. A transporter with PROBENECID PHASE_4 and PRATOSARTAN PHASE_3 as listed drugs. These are not antitumour uses, and loss of expression means it is not a drug target. Biomarker only.

Established ccRCC drug target (HIF-2 alpha). Open Targets rank is nine of the associated targets. Drug: BELZUTIFAN, APPROVAL. DepMap shows a positive ccRCC selectivity [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3] and it is not common essential. Only a fraction of ccRCC lines depend on it, and 2D culture understates HIF-2 biology.

Established ccRCC drug target. Many clinical-stage inhibitors are listed (for example GEDATOLISIB PHASE_3, DACTOLISIB PHASE_3, RIDAFOROLIMUS APPROVAL). DepMap shows strong ccRCC dependence [gene=MTOR; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-1.52], but it is common essential, so toxicity risk is high and the therapeutic window is narrow.

Established ccRCC target (VEGFR2). Approved agents include AXITINIB, PAZOPANIB HYDROCHLORIDE, TIVOZANIB, CABOZANTINIB S-MALATE, LENVATINIB MESYLATE and RAMUCIRUMAB (all APPROVAL), and SUNITINIB is PHASE_4. The target is endothelial and microenvironmental, so ccRCC cell lines are not dependent on it in DepMap (no selectivity, not common essential). This is an example of a valid target that a cell-line dependency screen cannot see.

Top Open Targets association [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466]. It is mutated in a large fraction of tumours [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483] and is a significant driver. Loss drives HIF stabilisation, which explains the CA9, EPAS1 and NNMT programme.

Second Open Targets association and a significant recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]. BAP1 and SETD2 are also significant recurrent drivers with strong Open Targets association. These tumour-suppressor losses are association and stratification genes and not directly druggable.

caveats: Open Targets scores are literature-weighted, and the top-ranked convergence genes (CA9, CD70, NNMT) have weak or no genetic association.

No leading convergence gene shows a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap; the exceptions are EPAS1 (partial) and MTOR (common essential). Antibody, ADC and imaging strategies for CA9 and CD70 do not need dependency, but this limits the small-molecule case.
DepMap and PRISM are 2D cell lines and miss HIF-2 and microenvironment biology (KDR is an example).
PRISM compounds with multiple targets, such as the CA9 hit, say little about the individual gene.
STRING interactions were not queried, and the convergence ranking was read only for the top twelve genes.
Open Targets drug stages are reported as returned and may include non-oncology indications.
